title: Replays of the earlier work, read through the chain
set_out: Keep the machines full on the earlier engine's series and the healthy plasmas, and record each result as it lands.

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out

entries.title: Alzheimer's blood, AIBL (OTH-082, DEV-REPLICATE-01 R4)
entries.what: All 726 AIBL arrays read by the one command; Alzheimer's and mild cognitive impairment against healthy controls.
entries.outcome: More neutrophils in Alzheimer's blood (d +0.30); no Met-A difference (d +0.09).

entries.title: Met-A's healthy middle line predicted from the array itself, synthetic (GRP-019, DEV-METAA-HEALTHY-01)
entries.what: Each array's own line and noise, measured at the atlas's firmly held sites, predict what a healthy sample reads on whole-sample Met-A.
entries.outcome: Through the one command, healthy reads within 0.005 of 1 on two of three synthetic arrays (0.007 off on the weakest), a loss still shows, and a real healthy blood moves from 1.11 to 1.01. The first synthetic test called the Met-A stage directly and does not count.

entries.title: R5, Crohn's disease and colitis in whole blood (OTH-082, DEV-REPLICATE-01)
entries.what: 382 bloods with Crohn's disease, colitis and none, each read by the one command.
entries.outcome: The disorder readings do not separate the groups; the smoking site and the neutrophil share do, as the known biology predicts.

entries.title: The healthy plasma band on sequencing, 30 plasmas (GRP-016, DEV-ONE-DRAW-01)
entries.what: Thirty healthy plasmas, each read end to end by the one command.
entries.outcome: The held error is nearly constant from person to person; IAM-A on cell-free DNA needs its own band; the atlas lacks one of plasma's main source cells.

entries.title: Why IAM-A reads low on plasma: synthetic test cfDNA 1 (GRP-016, DEV-ONE-DRAW-01)
entries.what: Constructed molecules from two cell types, mixed and cut short, each read by the one command.
entries.outcome: Both mixing and short molecules pull IAM-A down, neither through the atlas; each has its own fix to build.

entries.title: Where megakaryocyte DNA lands in plasma (GRP-016, DEV-ONE-DRAW-01)
entries.what: One donor's megakaryocytes read as plasma, then planted into a healthy plasma at known amounts, each through the one command.
entries.outcome: Megakaryocyte DNA lands on four atlas cells; their summed share is a stand-in until the cell enters the atlas.

entries.title: Met-A's healthy levels from the held error: layer 1 (GRP-019, DEV-METAA-HEALTHY-01)
entries.what: Each healthy cell type's level at the sites it holds predicted from its own held error, counted on its molecules, against IAM-Atlas v2.1.
entries.outcome: Within 0.02 in 54 of 56 cell types where the mark is held and 56 of 56 where it is held absent, once both are on the same scale; nothing fitted.

entries.title: A maintenance knockout read against the firm rate (PHY-006, PHY-050)
entries.what: The UHRF1 knockout and its control from the published leukemia study, counted by the chain.
entries.outcome: Held error 2.9 times the control's: maintenance failure makes holes in held molecules, the route the firm-rate derivation needs.

entries.title: The leukemia study's pass 1, 34 samples at 10 million read pairs (GRP-020, DEV-ALL-INFO-01)
entries.what: IAM-A's count by the one command on every sample of the published leukemia study with reads.
entries.outcome: The leukemias' held error sits above the cord-blood B cells'; the UHRF1 knockout moves it most.

entries.title: Met-A's derived neutrophil mark, versions 1 to 7 (GRP-019, DEV-METAA-HEALTHY-01 step 3)
entries.what: Seven ways of computing the neutrophil's healthy mark from its own molecules, each written before it was scored.
entries.outcome: Concluded: the marked side is predicted from the molecules, but the commissioned sites, chosen on the arrays they are scored against, read above each array's own curve; the commissioned baseline stays measured and the next version chooses its sites on the atlas.

entries.title: The provisional megakaryocyte column, versions 1 and 2 (GRP-016, DEV-ONE-DRAW-01)
entries.what: A megakaryocyte column beside the atlas built from donor 1's single cells and tested on donor 2's.
entries.outcome: Not met: single cells are too thin for a column; bulk purified data is needed and donor 3 stays unread.

entries.title: Replays on every array: prostate, tissues, stroke, Crohn's and colitis sorted cells (OTH-082, DEV-REPLICATE-01)
entries.what: The earlier engine's series read again on all their arrays after the unrun shards were found (lesson C42).
entries.outcome: The islands territory reads higher in prostate tumors and in glioblastoma; stroke and the sorted cells of Crohn's and colitis show nothing beyond chance.

entries.title: The gain side of the held error, counted by Stage Q2 (GRP-019, DEV-METAA-HEALTHY-01 layer 1)
entries.what: The counter now also counts a mark gained by error on molecules held unmarked, the mirror of the held error; it recovers known rates on constructed molecules.

entries.title: The loose share counted molecule by molecule (GRP-016, DEV-ONE-DRAW-01)
entries.what: Stage Q2 records a loose share that does not change when cell types mix, beside the tile share; synthetic test cfDNA 2 confirms it.

entries.title: Bone marrow read and flagged; series published only as value tables (GRP-020)
entries.what: Bone marrow and blood-and-marrow mixes are read on the full-atlas route and flagged, no longer refused at intake; series published only as value tables are read through the same values route.
entries.outcome: The value-table route matches a direct reading exactly.

entries.title: EPIC-Italy through the one command, first reading (GRP-018, DEV-FIRES-01)
entries.what: The first EPIC-Italy arrays read through the one command, beside the earlier engine's pattern recorded before reading.
entries.outcome: The earlier breast pattern repeats; the case arrays are of lower quality.

entries.title: Full-depth sequencing in pieces; the aligner index built once (GRP-020)
entries.what: A full-depth sample is cut into up to 20 ranges aligned on separate machines and merged; the aligner index is built once and kept as release files.
entries.outcome: The chunk plan uses every read pair once and a split-then-merged molecule file is byte-identical to the original.

entries.title: The paper's outline, Methods draft and generator (plan 50)
entries.what: The paper in the format of the leukemia study's own paper; every number read from the records at build time.
entries.outcome: Results fill in as each gated test lands.

entries.title: Provisional reference columns and public bigWig calls read by the chain (GRP-016, GRP-019)
entries.what: stage_provisional (a cell the atlas lacks, read in a second flagged deconvolution) and values_from_bigwig with the atlas's GRCh38 site key.
entries.outcome: Both used in the day's tests.

open_at_turnover: Running on GitHub's machines: 28 of the 30 healthy plasmas (sequencing to molecules, then the one command), and the rest of the earlier engine's series with raw arrays: Crohn's and colitis blood and sorted cells, stroke, prostate, pancreas, brain and aorta tissues, glioma patients' blood and cultured endothelial cells. Open: why EPIC-Italy's case arrays carry weaker signal.
